§7.3.9 Seals and Round Stamps

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-seals-and-round-stamps · text marks

✅ Normative

A seal or round stamp MUST be rendered as [seal: printed text], holding all of its legible rim and centre text in reading order, in a block separate from body prose. The bare [seal] MUST be used only when none of its text is legible.

A round or oval impression — an auditor's firm seal, a notary seal, a court seal — printed or inked on the page, usually beside a signature. Its text runs around the rim.

   ╭────────────╮        For, Caldrivane & Rao LLP
  ( CALDRIVANE &    )       Chartered Accountants
  (  RAO LLP     )       [signature]
   ╰────────────╯        A. N. Bhatt

Requirements

  • The seal MUST NOT be dropped. It is the page's proof of authority, the same kind of fact as a signature, and its text is often the only place the firm's name is printed.
  • Its text MUST be kept verbatim and in a readable order — in the samples, upper rim, then centre, then lower rim — including a word the rim cuts short. Illegible characters are left out, never guessed.
  • The seal MUST be its own block, never part of a sentence beside it.
  • A stamp that lands on a table is kept out of the grid — see Handwriting and Stamps§9.6.5.
  • A signature written across the seal is a separate mark — see Signatures§7.3.10.

✅ Sample — an auditor's seal beside a signature

A blue circular seal: CALDRIVANE & RAO LLP along the upper rim, H&R over LLP in the centre, and CHARTERED ACCOUNTAN along the lower rim — the rim runs out before the word ends. Beside it, a handwritten signature over a printed name, designation and registration numbers. Also the sample for a signature whose name is printed beneath it — see Signatures§7.3.10.

✅ Sample — a firm stamp with a signature inside it

A purple round stamp at the foot of a scanned letter: KESSLER & VANE on the upper rim, CHARTERED ACCOUNTANTS in the centre, FRN-408217E • ASTILBE on the lower rim, and a handwritten mark through its centre. The letterhead prints a logo on the left and two address blocks on the right.
